title: An invertible sheaf on an algebraic scheme over an infinite field is generated by dim(X) + 1 sections
author: The Stacks Project Authors
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
difficulty_reason: Over an infinite field k, for an algebraic k-scheme X and an invertible sheaf L generated by a linear map V to the global sections, the lemma produces a subspace W of V of dimension at most dim(X) + 1 which still generates L (statement lines 4259-4266). The proof is an induction on dim(X) driven by a nonvanishing condition: for every point x the composite of the given map with evaluation at x and reduction to the residue field is nonzero, and this is used twice. In the zero dimensional base case, X has finitely many points and infinitude of k allows a single vector on which none of the finitely many functionals vanishes (proof lines 4269-4282). In the induction step the author picks one point on each top dimensional irreducible component, chooses a vector nonvanishing at all of them, takes its zero scheme Z and observes that dim(Z) is strictly smaller than dim(X), applies the induction hypothesis to Z, and concludes that the span of the resulting subspace with that single vector generates L (proof lines 4285-4294). The claim is H2: a short induction whose content is the finite-avoidance choice of the vector and the strict dimension drop at the zero scheme.
